facts.text: Liaison poll Oct. 8-9: Chow 51, Bradford 46 among decided and leaning voters
Liaison margin of error plus or minus 3.1 points, 19 times out of 20
Chow's Liaison lead narrowed from eight points to five after Chris Alexander left the race
Nanos poll for CP24/CTV: Chow 51, Bradford 47 among decided voters, 17 per cent undecided
Renters back Chow 57-40; homeowners back Bradford 50-45
Chow approval 52 per cent, disapproval 43
Bradford 37 per cent favourable, 40 unfavourable
Record advance vote: 222,550 ballots over six days Oct. 6-11, per City of Toronto
Election day Monday Oct. 26, 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.; 361 candidates certified Aug. 24
Chow and Bradford certified mayoral candidates, nominated May 25 and May 1
Final debate Oct. 15 hosted by Rotman and TVO, moderated by Steve Paikin
Both candidates campaigned in Scarborough this week on transit and housing costs/spending
Advance turnout up nearly 92 per cent from 115,911 advance votes in 2022
Oct. 11 busiest advance day at 53,363, highest one-day total since amalgamation
Chow said voters told her they voted for her; Bradford said turnout shows change is coming
Advance numbers do not show which candidates were chosen
CP24 gave the advance total as 225,550, not matching the city's 222,550
CityNews, Global News and the Toronto Sun carry the city's 222,550 figure
City news release list shows no advance-turnout release after Oct. 13
CBC: advance turnout nearly 72 per cent above 2023 byelection's 129,745
Liaison: Downtown 40 per cent of advance vote; North York share up, Scarborough down
Eglinton-Lawrence led wards with about 15,000 advance ballots; citywide participation 10.4 per cent
No city statement correcting or restating the 222,550 figure found

missed.text: Liaison regional numbers: Bradford leads Scarborough 50-47 and Etobicoke 59-38; Chow leads Downtown 57-39 and North York 50-46
Nanos regional numbers: Bradford leads Etobicoke/York 42.2-39 and North York 45.6-38.8; Chow leads Toronto/East York 49-30
Endorsements: Geddy Lee for Bradford; Jim Cuddy and LIUNA Local 183 for Chow
Chow's Oct. 11 message: lower grocery bills, 10 transit rides per week then free, renter protections, more housing, seniors' supports
